description:
Export the product catalog to `/work/export/catalog.csv`, replacing the previous export.

Read the catalog with `catalog_list` (`svc.catalogList` in TypeScript), one page at a time: `limit` is always 20 and `offset` is 0, 20, 40, and so on. Stop after the first page that holds fewer than 20 products (possibly none). Give every call a 400 millisecond timeout.

A page read that fails with a transient kind (`Timeout`, `Unavailable`, `RateLimited`) is tried again: wait 100 milliseconds after the failure and read the same page again; if that fails transiently too, wait 300 milliseconds and read it a third time. A page read that fails with any other kind, or fails three times, ends the export: print one line naming the failure to standard error, leave `/work/export/` exactly as it was, and exit with status 4.

The catalog changes while you read it, so a product (identified by `sku`) can appear on more than one page. Use, for each sku, the record with the highest `version`. Leave out every product whose chosen record has `active` false.

The export is CSV: a header line `sku,name,price`, then one line per product, sorted by sku in byte order. `price` is `price_cents` as a decimal with exactly two digits after the point (`1999` is `19.99`, `5` is `0.05`). A field that contains a comma, a double quote or a line break is enclosed in double quotes, with each double quote inside it doubled. Lines end with a newline.

Replace the old `/work/export/catalog.csv` in one step, so that a reader sees either the old file or the complete new one, never a partial file; leave nothing else in `/work/export/`. On success print `exported N products` with the number of product lines and exit with status 0.

Product.type: {sku: Str, name: Str, price_cents: Int, version: Int, active: Bool}
Product.doc: One catalog record; a higher version of the same sku is newer.

capabilities.description: Reads up to `limit` catalog records starting at `offset`.
